title: AdMem: Expectation-Grounded Procedural Memory for Long-Horizon Task-Solving Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.20605v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: An agent that carries memory across tasks is only as good as the entries it keeps. We begin from an observation that is easy to reproduce and uncomfortable for the field: naively accumulating cross-task experience can make an agent \emph{worse} than one with no memory at all. On AgentBoard, a workflow-induction memory solves fewer tasks than a memoryless ReAct agent in seven of eight domains, and a per-step procedural store with no surrounding structure loses half of ReAct's completions on Jericho. We argue that the missing ingredients are per-action credit assignment and an explicit life cycle for stored entries, and present AdMem, which supplies both. Before each action the actor commits to an expected outcome; a concurrently running critic scores the realized outcome against that expectation and writes a procedural entry carrying a binary reward and a reflection, so credit lands on the action that earned it and no environment reward i

translated_title: AdMem：面向长程任务求解智能体的基于期望的程序性记忆
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.20605v1 公告类型：新 摘要：一个跨任务携带记忆的智能体，其好坏取决于它所保存的条目。我们从一个易于复现却令该领域不安的观察出发：天真地积累跨任务经验可能会使智能体比完全没有记忆的智能体表现更差。在 AgentBoard 上，工作流归纳式记忆在八个领域中的七个里解决的任务数少于无记忆的 ReAct 智能体；而在 Jericho 上，缺乏周围结构的逐步程序性存储损失了 ReAct 一半的任务完成数。我们认为缺失的关键要素是逐动作的信用分配以及存储条目的显式生命周期，并提出了同时提供这两者的 AdMem。在每次执行动作之前，执行者承诺一个预期结果；一个并发运行的评判者将实际结果与该预期进行对比评分，并写入一条携带二元奖励和反思的程序性条目，从而使信用归属于产生该结果的动作，而无需环境奖励……（原文此处截断）
tldr: 提出了 AdMem，通过让执行者在动作前承诺预期结果、由并发评判者对照预期打分并写入携带二元奖励与反思的程序性条目，实现了逐动作信用分配和存储条目的显式生命周期，解决了朴素跨任务记忆积累反而使智能体性能变差的问题。
en_tdlr: AdMem grounds procedural memory in per-action expectations—an actor commits to an expected outcome before acting and a concurrent critic scores the realized result against it—enabling per-action credit assignment and an explicit entry life cycle that fixes the problem of naive cross-task memory accumulation making agents worse than memoryless ones.
